Research developing autocomplete capabilities for for ddflow cli commands and ID and options and create phase and tasks to impenet this

data.claim: A stdlib-only, generated completion works: (1) static command/option tree is exported from build_parser() into per-shell scripts (bash, zsh, fish) at install/upgrade time; (2) IDs come from a read-only sqlite3 query of .ddflow/index.db-* items table, not from running ddflow; (3) argcomplete is not adopted as a runtime dependency. A per-TAB 'ddflow' subprocess is not viable.
data.falsifier: If a bash/zsh completion that shells out to python -c 'import sqlite3' still exceeds ~100 ms per TAB, or if the newest-index heuristic offers stale ids in a repo with several index files, the sqlite approach fails and a pre-generated ids cache file refreshed by the post-merge hook is needed.
data.mechanism: ddflow is pure argparse (SuggestingParser, build_parser() in surfaces/cli.py, subcommands registered from surfaces/parsers/*, compat aliases via _WordsRecorder/_hide_from_abbreviation). pyproject declares exactly two runtime deps (jinja2, tomlkit) by policy; argcomplete and shtab are not installed. 'ddflow --version' takes ~1.0 s and importing ddflow.surfaces.cli ~0.83 s (ddflow.api imports dominate), 'ddflow list/show' ~4.7 s on this loaded machine, so argcomplete-style per-TAB invocation would add 1-5 s per keypress. The derived index .ddflow/index.db-<code fingerprint> is plain sqlite: items(id,kind,title,state,needs,tags,...) 3488 rows, count query 0.0 s, openable read-only with stdlib sqlite3. Index name embeds code_fingerprint(), so a stale file can exist; the completer must pick the newest by mtime or fall back to nothing.

data.question: How should ddflow offer shell completion (commands, options, IDs) given its argparse CLI, two-runtime-dependency policy and slow startup?
sources: ddflow/surfaces/cli.py build_parser; ddflow/surfaces/registry.py; pyproject.toml dependencies; ddflow/infra/store.py index.db naming

data.body: Research R-shell-completion-design. Stdlib only (two-runtime-dependency policy): a command tree exported from build_parser(), generated scripts per shell, IDs read from the derived sqlite index without importing ddflow.api (startup is ~1 s), install only with the operator's consent. Every new CLI verb touches golden snapshots, README tables and pins: run 'pytest tests/test_scenarios.py -m slow' and 'ddflow pins regenerate --check' before merge.
data.title: Shell completion: commands, options, values and IDs for bash, zsh and fish

data.body: Ask the operator, with defaults: (1) shells: bash+zsh+fish (default) or bash only first; (2) install: explicit 'ddflow completion install' plus a doctor note, never automatic (default); (3) stdlib-only generated scripts (default, per R-shell-completion-design) vs argcomplete as an optional extra; (4) ID source: read-only sqlite of .ddflow/index.db-* (default) vs a cache file refreshed by the post-merge hook; (5) which values complete: ids of every record kind, enums, gate names, phases, agents. Record each answer as D-completion-*.
data.title: DECIDE: shell completion scope, install policy and ID source (operator questions with defaults)

data.body: Pure function parser -> JSON-able tree: subcommand words (incl. compat aliases but not hidden old flags per _hide_from_abbreviation), options with arity and choices, and a value kind per argument (id:task|bug|phase|..., enum, path, free). Walks argparse internals once; no side effects; no import of ddflow.api beyond parser building. Tests: every option of every real subcommand appears; hidden/compat flags are not offered; stable ordering.
data.title: Export the CLI command tree from build_parser(): commands, options, choices, aliases, value kinds

data.body: New verb 'ddflow completion SHELL' prints a script to stdout (managed templates under ddflow/templates/completion, one per shell, each under 20 KB). Commands and options complete from the embedded tree with no ddflow subprocess; value kinds call the fast ID helper. Tests run bash and zsh -c with a faked COMP_WORDS where those shells exist, otherwise record unavailable. Regenerate golden snapshots, README command table and pins.
data.title: ddflow completion <bash|zsh|fish>: generate the completion script from the tree

data.body: Stdlib-only module opened read-only (sqlite3 file:...?mode=ro) on the newest .ddflow/index.db-* by mtime (the name embeds code_fingerprint(), so several can exist); items.id by kind/state, bugs, research, decisions, lessons; finds the primary checkout from a worktree. Returns nothing (never an error) when no index exists. Budget test: cold python start plus query under 100 ms on this repo's 3.5k items, via python -S -c. Falsifier from R-shell-completion-design: if it exceeds the budget, fall back to a cache file refreshed by the post-merge hook.
data.title: Fast value helper: ids, states, phases, gates from the sqlite index in under 100 ms without importing ddflow.api

data.body: Map each option and positional to a value kind in the tree and complete it: record ids by kind (task show/claim/complete/gate ..., bug show/fixed, phase), enum choices from argparse, gate names from the configured pipeline, phases and tags, files and directories for path options. Positional id completion must respect the verb (claim offers open items; bug fixed offers open bugs).
data.title: Complete option values: --state, --phase, --item, --gate, --kind, --agent, paths for --globs and --repo

data.body: install writes the script to the shell's completion directory (bash-completion dir, zsh fpath, fish completions) and prints the one line to source if no standard dir exists; uninstall removes only what it wrote; dry run by default or a clear confirm. 'ddflow doctor' notes when no completion is installed (advice, never a failure); 'adopt' and 'upgrade' mention it. Never installs unasked (project rule on companions).
data.title: ddflow completion install/uninstall and a doctor note; install only with the operator's consent

data.body: Ratchet: a new subcommand or option added to build_parser() shows up in the generated completions with no extra change (fails otherwise); every shell script parses (bash -n, zsh -n, fish -n where present, else unavailable); latency budget for command and id completion. Run the slow scenarios and 'ddflow pins regenerate --check'.
data.title: Conformance and performance tests: the tree matches the parser, new commands appear automatically, latency budget

data.body: Document the verbs, supported shells, what completes, the stdlib-only decision, the latency budget and how to uninstall. README is ddflow-managed (see P-readme): follow its generated-table rules.
data.title: Docs: README row, 'ddflow help completion' topic and install guide
